title: Gates Urges CEOs on AI Safety as Oversight Calls Grow
key_facts: Bill Gates is preparing to expand his AI safety campaign, personally pressing business leaders and weighing a significant commitment of resources; the Axios report gives no funding figure or timetable.
He told one adviser: "I can reach CEOs on this better than you can."
He is concerned about fast-advancing AI capabilities, security incidents and weak government oversight.
He has discussed the risks with tech executives, researchers and safety advocates, including Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei.

On NBC's Meet the Press on 27 Sep 2026 he urged congressional action, said industry self-regulation is insufficient, and warned international AI cooperation would be harder than Cold War nuclear arms agreements.
The Trump administration favors voluntary industry safeguards; major tech companies recently signed a safety pact at the White House.
On 7 Oct 2026 Sen. Maria Cantwell (D-Wash.) released a framework calling for enforceable federal AI safety standards, testing and independent audits.

Axios reports that people who spoke with Gates see the advocacy partly as an effort to rebuild his legacy after scrutiny of his past association with Jeffrey Epstein, which he called 'a huge mistake' in August.
quote_evidence: I can reach CEOs on this better than you can.
why_it_matters_hint: A famous philanthropist may press tech chiefs harder on AI safety, against an administration that prefers voluntary safeguards.
notes: Read in full from Yahoo News (Theodore Bunker, 15 Oct 2026), which cites Axios; the Axios and Washington Times pages themselves were not readable. No funding figure or timetable is given. Context in the text: Gates on NBC Meet the Press (27 Sep) said industry self-regulation is not enough; Sen. Maria Cantwell released a federal AI safety framework on 7 Oct.
